# Final Review Proposal
**Producer:** agent:codex/gpt-5.4

## Summary

`git diff` was empty in the working tree, so I reviewed the current shrimp stage-model implementation end-to-end (`biology.rs`, `shrimp.rs`, `save.rs`, snapshot/API/TUI surfaces). I found three substantive issues: the new lifecycle knobs are not wired to presets/scenario materialization, legacy maturation timing is not migrated into the new stage fields, and the newly added `ShrimpRuntimeParams` are never validated on load.

## Amendments

1. `crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:135-155` still exposes only the old shrimp species fields, and `crates/tank_scenarios/src/lib.rs:511-523` builds `ShrimpRuntimeParams` by filling every new stage-structured knob from `..ShrimpRuntimeParams::default()`. At the same time the legacy `process_params.shrimp_juvenile_maturation_days` is still loaded in `crates/tank_scenarios/src/lib.rs:420-423`, but stage promotion now reads only `state.shrimp_params` in `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:610-683`. The result is that scenario/preset lifecycle tuning silently does nothing: maturation timing, molt timing, clutch sizing, and sub-adult sensitivity all fall back to hard-coded defaults instead of scenario data.
   Rationale: This breaks the task’s “parameterized and tunable” requirement for newly seeded scenarios and makes existing preset knobs misleading.
2. The v4->v5 migration in `crates/tank_core/src/save.rs:408-573` rewrites `state.animal`, but it never derives `shrimp_params.juvenile_to_subadult_days` / `subadult_to_adult_days` from the legacy `process_params.shrimp_juvenile_maturation_days`. Missing stage fields then deserialize to the defaults in `crates/tank_core/src/types/biology.rs:347-352`, while runtime promotion consults only those new fields in `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:610-683`. Any older save with a non-default maturation schedule will therefore load with a silently changed 30+20 day lifecycle, so old saves do not actually migrate cleanly.
   Rationale: This is a backward-compatibility bug: legacy saves can load successfully but simulate different population dynamics than the file encoded before migration.
3. `SaveFile::into_engine` relies on invariant enforcement for load-time validation (`crates/tank_core/src/save.rs:215-226`), but `validate_invariants_inner` returns after checking `process_params` and never validates any of the new `ShrimpRuntimeParams` fields declared in `crates/tank_core/src/types/biology.rs:165-217` (`crates/tank_core/src/invariants.rs:215-252`). A current-schema save or API load can therefore set impossible species settings and the engine will accept them, after which `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:610-683` and `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:927-969` silently clamp or run with nonsensical stage timing/temperature/GH behavior instead of rejecting bad input.
   Rationale: The stage-model added many new runtime knobs, but malformed current-schema data is not guarded. That is a real robustness gap for save loading and any external JSON caller.
